reader_guide: Read the overall grade as a judgment of the code on the founder’s Stage 1 phone, not as approval for a public release. The six letter grades describe what the source shows today. The three risk grades identify behavior that needs a phone test before anyone can call it safe. Start with REF-01 and REF-02: they concern the capture thread and a polish process that could remain stuck after a take. Each finding includes lines to open, the likely effect, and a test that could disprove it. The roadmap orders changes by dependency; it does not imply that every item has caused a reported failure. The strengths matter too: the session has one owner, polish usually fails back to the user’s words, insertion checks the editor’s text, and privacy has explicit enforcers. This was a read-only review. No build, device run, network capture, or full line-by-line review of every inventory file was performed. The `not_assessed` entries mark those limits and the Stage 2 work that must not lower this Stage 1 grade.

overall_grade.rationale: This is professional senior engineering at a Stage 1 proof of concept, not AI slop. The process boundaries, single session owner, typed fallbacks, insertion checks, model verification, and privacy filters are substantive. The main debt is a rare allocation on the capture thread, an unbounded native warm-up teardown path, additive startup waits, and ownership and test claims that have drifted. Public-production readiness is unproven.
overall_grade.confidence_rationale: The central control paths and their supporting tests were inspected, but the sandbox prohibited builds and phone runs, and some inventory files received only a bounded scan.

dimensions.name: Architecture integrity
dimensions.justification: The current shell is 240 lines and the Android service is 259 lines; the mass now sits in the 1,255-line coordinator, 1,000-line audio service, 817-line overlay, 770-line Dictionary screen, and 762-line settings pages. One owner admits a take and delegates capture, polish, and finalization. History recovery is still initiated by both the session owner and the History view model.

best_example.why_exemplary: Admission and terminal arbitration have one owner and one take identity.

worst_violation.confidence_rationale: HistoryViewModel.kt L59-L66 starts the same stale-row and rescued-word recovery.
worst_violation.counterfactual: Opening History around a take starts duplicate recovery work, and a future change to one recovery path can leave the other behaving differently.
worst_violation.counterfactual_rationale: The two callers independently invoke the same repository recovery and telemetry methods.
worst_violation.falsifiability: Instrument the repository with call counters, create the session owner while opening History, and show that each recovery operation runs only once.

dimensions.name: Concurrency discipline
dimensions.justification: Scopes, take IDs, and binder handoffs are generally explicit. The live-event publisher has one allocation branch reachable from the capture loop, despite the capture-thread rule.

best_example.why_exemplary: The recurring heartbeat uses a preallocated slot and wakes a separate binder worker.

worst_violation.confidence_rationale: AudioCaptureService.kt L695-L703 calls this from the capture loop; the failed-claim branch constructs an Event.Live and a queue node.
worst_violation.counterfactual: If the event worker falls behind across takes, the capture thread allocates at the first live frame and can suffer a pause during a latency-sensitive read loop.
worst_violation.counterfactual_rationale: An occupied slot forces the explicit allocation branch. A visible audio glitch still requires runtime measurement.
worst_violation.falsifiability: Hold delivery of take A's Live event, start take B on the same audio service, and measure allocations on AudioCaptureThread while B goes live; zero allocations would disprove the claim.
worst_violation.concurrency_interleaving: 1. Take A publishes Live and leaves the slot READY. 2. The publisher worker is delayed before clearing that slot. 3. Take A ends and take B starts while the service remains alive. 4. Take B's capture thread calls publishLive. 5. Its CAS fails and it constructs Event.Live on the capture thread.

dimensions.name: Testability
dimensions.justification: The suite includes a real cross-UID editor outcome test and injectable session seams. One source guard says it protects an allocation-free live path while accepting the allocating fallback.

best_example.snippet:
@Test
    fun aSideButtonTakeLandsInTheFocusedEditorExactlyOnce() {
        val expected = expectedFinal()
        val run = SideButtonRun()
        startRig(twoFields = false)
        run.recordOneTake(stage = {})
        val row = run.awaitFinalRow()
        val text = receipt(PasteTargetActivity.RECEIPT_NAME)
        assertEquals("the editor's whole text is the literal expectation", expected, text)
        assertEquals("the words appear exactly once", 1, occurrences(text, expected.trim()))
        assertEquals("the owner recorded the commit route", InsertionResults.COMMITTED, row.insertionResult)
        DebugLogger.log("VoicePipelineDeviceTest", "sideButtonTake chars=${text.length} result=${row.insertionResult}")
best_example.why_exemplary: It checks the text received by an editor in a separate test app, not merely a binder call.

worst_violation.snippet:
val publisher = File("src/main/java/com/envi/wispr/audio/TakeEventPublisher.kt").readText()
        val publishLive = member(publisher, "fun publishLive(")
        val claim = publishLive.indexOf("liveState.compareAndSet(TICK_IDLE, TICK_WRITING)")
        assertTrue("the slot is claimed", claim >= 0)
        val built = publishLive.indexOf("Event.Live(")
        assertTrue("an event is built only in the fallback, after the claim", built > claim && publishLive.substring(claim, built).contains("} else {"))
        assertFalse("no log on the Live path", publishLive.contains("DebugLogger"))
worst_violation.rule_violated: .claude/rules/testing-philosophy.md RULE: every-test-declares-which-of-four-things-it-protects; named principle: a test's assertion must match its claimed behavior
worst_violation.confidence_rationale: The test is named goingLiveAllocatesNothingOnTheCaptureThread but requires Event.Live to be built in the fallback.
worst_violation.counterfactual: The test stays green while the rare path allocates on the capture thread, so a reviewer can mistake it for proof of a stronger guarantee.
worst_violation.counterfactual_rationale: The assertion checks where allocation occurs, not whether it occurs on that thread.
worst_violation.falsifiability: Hold the Live slot occupied and run this test against the current publisher. If the test fails because of that allocation, the finding is wrong.
worst_violation.concurrency_interleaving: 1. The first take leaves Live in the slot. 2. The worker has not cleared it. 3. A following take enters the allocating fallback. 4. The source assertion still passes because Event.Live appears after the CAS.

dimensions.name: Code hygiene and maintainability
dimensions.justification: Provider wire decisions and session helpers have clear owners. SettingsPages.kt still places seven independent settings pages and their helpers in one 762-line file; this is low-risk maintenance debt, not a heart-path failure.

best_example.why_exemplary: One exhaustive routing table keeps provider identity decisions in one place.

worst_violation.rule_violated: Named engineering principle: one screen family per source owner; .claude/rules/architecture-rules.md RULE: keep-central-types-thin
worst_violation.confidence_rationale: The inventory measures 762 lines; this file declares Storage, WhatsNew, Appearance, Microphone, Sounds, Clipboard, Privacy, Licenses, and Permissions pages.
worst_violation.counterfactual: A developer changing microphone routing or privacy copy must navigate unrelated pages and imports in the same file.
worst_violation.counterfactual_rationale: The file is an aggregation of separate screens rather than a shared settings primitive.
worst_violation.falsifiability: Run `rg -n '^internal fun .*Page' app/src/main/java/com/envi/wispr/ui/SettingsPages.kt`; if it declares only one page family, this finding is wrong.

dimensions.name: API surface
dimensions.justification: The production take binds a five-operation AIDL surface and most app declarations use internal visibility. An older AIDL comment gives an inaccurate reason for the append-only rule; the rule itself remains sound.

best_example.why_exemplary: The session owner receives only the operations it uses.

    // by transaction number, and renumbering breaks it at runtime with no compile error.
worst_violation.rule_violated: .claude/rules/architecture-rules.md RULE: aidl-is-append-only; named principle: contract comments must describe the actual client packaging
worst_violation.confidence_rationale: The current rule explicitly says the test APK defines no AIDL classes of its own and reordering alone does not mismatch transaction numbers in this setup.
worst_violation.counterfactual: A maintainer may make compatibility decisions from an outdated explanation of how this test client binds.
worst_violation.counterfactual_rationale: The comment describes independently packaged transaction numbering, while the current rule documents shared generated classes.

dimensions.name: Performance and latency
dimensions.justification: The normal first-frame times reported in current-state are short, but the source permits additive pre-capture waits: settings can use 2 seconds, matcher and policy 1 second, then journal admission 300 milliseconds. The actual S26 tail and insertion latency need measurement.

best_example.why_exemplary: The event worker parks without an idle polling timer.

worst_violation.rule_violated: Named engineering principle: independent pre-capture limb deadlines should share one trigger-to-frame budget
worst_violation.confidence_rationale: The source orders the waits; Coordinator constants set 2 seconds and 1 second, and journal admission adds a later 300-millisecond bound.
worst_violation.counterfactual: If independent readers are slow on a cold take, the lips can remain in Starting for roughly 3.3 seconds before the audio bind is requested.
worst_violation.counterfactual_rationale: Each bounded wait starts after the preceding stage rather than consuming one admission deadline. The measured frequency on the founder’s phone is unknown.
worst_violation.falsifiability: Delay both settings answers to their bound, the matcher or policy to its bound, and journal admission to its bound; measure bindRequested from the accepted trigger. A result within 2 seconds disproves the additive path.

dimensions.name: Resource lifecycle
dimensions.justification: The Bluetooth hold is intentional, limited to eligible successful endings, and has an expiry and close path. A native polish warm-up that stalls before a request is counted has no hard deadline at service teardown.

best_example.snippet:
started = hold
        heldSinkType = sink.type
        heldSinkName = sink.productName?.toString().orEmpty()
        warmHold = hold
        if (!hold.start()) {
            clearHoldBookkeeping()
            return false
        }
        val expiry = Runnable { locked { if (warmHold === hold) hold.end(WarmHold.END_EXPIRED) } }
        holdExpiry = expiry
        scheduler.postDelayed(expiry, WarmHold.HOLD_MS)
best_example.why_exemplary: The decided silent hold has a named owner and scheduled expiry.

worst_violation.confidence_rationale: The queued close cannot run ahead of a stuck load on the single executor. Whether the vendor can stall in load on this phone was not tested.
worst_violation.counterfactual: After a take ends, a stalled warm-up can leave the polish worker and model load resident until Android kills the process.
worst_violation.counterfactual_rationale: Warm-up does not increment activeLocalRequests or arm the generation deadline; the orderly close is queued behind it.
worst_violation.falsifiability: Inject a native-load stall before a polish request, unbind the service, and show that the polish process exits and releases residency within a fixed bound.
worst_violation.concurrency_interleaving: 1. The binder enqueues warm-up on the single executor. 2. The worker enters a stalled native model load. 3. The session ends without a local request, so activeLocalRequests is zero. 4. onDestroy takes the orderly branch and queues close behind the stalled load. 5. The close cannot execute.

dimensions.name: Security and privacy
dimensions.justification: The reviewed source keeps model files app-private and hash-verified, stores provider keys under Android Keystore, filters PostHog and Sentry fields, and refuses inference if the GenieX log silencer cannot be installed. Network packets and vendor behavior were not observed.

best_example.why_exemplary: Readiness depends on the exact manifest, file set, byte counts, and SHA-256 hashes.

refactor_targets.title: Remove the Live fallback allocation from the capture thread
refactor_targets.fix_shape: Replace Event.Live construction in TakeEventPublisher.publishLive with preallocated handoff storage that can replace an undelivered Live from an ended take without allocating on AudioCaptureThread. Keep binder delivery on the worker. Change CaptureThreadPathTest to stage an occupied slot and assert zero capture-thread allocations, while checking that the current take's Live event arrives.

refactor_targets.title: Give local model warm-up a hard teardown bound
refactor_targets.fix_shape: Track warm-up as its own in-flight operation in PolishService, arm an independent hard deadline for S1GenieXRuntime.load, and end the polish process if the service is destroyed while that load cannot close. Do not queue the only close behind a worker known to be stuck. Add an injected blocking-load service test for teardown and process exit.

refactor_targets.title: Use one pre-capture deadline for independent preparation
refactor_targets.rule_violated: Named engineering principle: independent pre-capture limb deadlines should share one trigger-to-frame budget
refactor_targets.fix_shape: In TakeStartPreparer, start the policy read and journal admission wait when a take is admitted, allow the terms-dependent matcher to start as soon as terms answer, and evaluate all results against one absolute admission deadline. Preserve the existing fallback values and cancellation checks. Record accepted-to-bind timing on the S26.

refactor_targets.title: Give startup History recovery one application owner
refactor_targets.fix_shape: Introduce one application-owned HistoryRecoveryCoordinator in history/ that runs stale-row recovery, rescued-word recovery, and their telemetry once per process. Have session startup and HistoryViewModel request that coordinator's completion or state. Delete their duplicate recovery bodies; leave History-only wordless-row pruning with the History owner.

refactor_targets.title: Separate unrelated settings pages
refactor_targets.rule_violated: Named engineering principle: one screen family per source owner
refactor_targets.fix_shape: Move MicrophonePage and its device callback and rows into MicrophonePage.kt; move PrivacyPage, StoragePage, and LicensesPage into their own page files. Leave shared settings components in SettingsComponents.kt and remove the moved declarations and imports from SettingsPages.kt.

refactor_targets.title: Correct AIDL compatibility comments
refactor_targets.rule_violated: .claude/rules/architecture-rules.md RULE: aidl-is-append-only; named principle: contract comments must describe the actual client packaging
refactor_targets.fix_shape: Update the older transaction-number comments in the audio, ASR, and VAD AIDL files to state the current reason for preserving called signatures: the installed test APK uses generated classes from the app APK. Keep every method and its order unchanged, and retain the append-only rule.

phased_roadmap.title: Close capture and lifecycle risks
phased_roadmap.rationale: These changes have no dependencies and protect the capture path, release the polish process, and give History recovery one owner.

phased_roadmap.title: Reduce pre-capture tail latency
phased_roadmap.rationale: With recovery removed from the session owner, the preparation path can use one measured admission budget.

phased_roadmap.title: Pay down local maintenance debt
phased_roadmap.rationale: These source-organization and contract-comment changes have low user blast radius.

strengths.pattern_name: Single take admission and target pin
strengths.why_preserve: One state transition creates the take identity, arbiter, and editor target.
Invalid or blank answers produce deterministic text and a defect.

strengths.pattern_name: One insertion write followed by evidence
strengths.why_preserve: A write attempt is recorded before calling the editor, preventing a blind second write.
A receipt alone cannot make an altered or partial model ready.
Provider keys are encrypted with authenticated encryption before entering app-private storage.
The send seam clears messages, user and request objects, and judges tags and extras.
The decided hold is limited to selected successful Bluetooth endings.
